# Minsky moment

Stability is destabilising. A long calm period persuades borrowers and lenders that risk has fallen, so they take more of it, until the structure cannot carry itself.

## Three stages

1. Hedge finance: income covers interest and principal.
2. Speculative finance: income covers interest only, and the principal must be rolled over.
3. Ponzi finance: income covers neither, and the borrower depends on rising asset prices to refinance.

## The moment

The moment is the point at which lenders stop rolling debt over. Assets have to be sold to meet payments, prices fall, and falling prices force more selling. The upswing took years; the reversal takes weeks.

Belief feeds on itself here, which is why I want a note on [[Reflexivity]]. Part of the [[Long debt cycle]].
